newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine tax accord will miss IMF deadline.
newsitem.headline: Philippine tax accord will miss IMF deadline.

text.p: The Philippine Senate will not be able to pass a crucial tax reform bill by this week, the deadline set under and International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme, Senate ways and means committee chairman Juan Ponce Enrile said on Wednesday.
"We cannot finish it (this week). The most we can do is try to finish it not later than end of August," Enrile told reporters after updating legislators and Cabinet members on the status of the bill.
The bill is the last of a package of major tax since President Fidel Ramos took office in 1992 and its passage will allow the end of 32 years of IMF supervision.
But Congress is scheduled to go into recess on Thursday and reconvene in the third week of July.
The bill, which aims to generate 18 billion pesos a year, would expand the number of people who pay income tax and overhaul the corporate income tax structure.
The Senate is still deliberating on its bill. One already passed by the House of Representatives has been opposed in the government which argues it has too many loopholes.
Once the Senate passes its version, a bicameral committee will be formed to sort out the differences.
Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said the government has not decided whether to let the IMF programme lapse or seek an extension.
A meeting with Senate and House leaders would be set to decide on the matter.

"My own inclination is to go for an extension so that we don't end up with an IMF exit that has a lingering policy measure that is important for us to pass in order for the economy to have a sound revenue foundation," de Ocampo said.
President Fidel Ramos earlier said he opted for an extension.
The government has been trumpeting the expected exit from IMF as the next step in the country's march to joining the ranks of Asia's tiger economies.
But analysts said a delay in quitting the programme was not so much a concern than the possibility the tax reforms might be watered down.
